operations.summary: What this API key can do
operations.description: The key's scopes, the plan tier, the rate limit, and which send-time safety checks apply to the account. Requires no scope: it exists so a client can plan its calls instead of discovering scopes through 403s.

Usage and plan limits in the same shape as Resend's GET /usage: emails in the last 24 hours and this month (with the reset time), contacts, segments, broadcasts this month, domains, and the rate limit. A null limit means no cap. Received mail does not count against the email limit, and prepaid credits are an extra field. On a team, the email quota and broadcast cap follow the team owner's plan and the domain limit the team's plan. Requires no scope.

Sending and deliverability totals for the account, plus a 30-day daily series. Pass days and/or domain to add a `window` object holding exact counts for that window and sending domain, aggregated in the database rather than sampled from the event log.

queryParams.name: days
queryParams.description: Window in days (1-90) for the `window` block. Present in the response only when days or domain is given.

queryParams.name: domain
queryParams.description: Restrict the `window` block to one sending domain, by name or id.

operations.description: Generate a new API key. The full key value is returned only once in the response. Store it securely.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: Optional list of scopes to restrict the key. Available: email:send, email:read, domain:read, domain:write, contact:read, contact:write, form:read, form:write, webhook:read, webhook:write, logs:read, inbound:read, inbound:delete, team:read, team:manage, apikey:manage. If omitted the key gets the default set: everything except logs:read, inbound:read, inbound:delete, team:read, team:manage and apikey:manage. Listing, creating or revoking keys through the API requires apikey:manage.

operations.summary: Claim a domain held by another account
operations.description: Checks the claim TXT record and moves a never-verified domain from the account that holds it to the caller's team, with its verification reset and any mail the previous holder still had queued through it cancelled. POST /v1/domains answers 409 with code domain_claimable and the record when this applies. 422 claim_record_missing when the record is not visible, 503 dns_unavailable when the lookup itself failed. The previous holder is notified. Requires the domain:write scope; 20 checks per hour per team.

operations.summary: Get the claim record for a domain
operations.description: The TXT record a team publishes to prove DNS control before claiming a domain another account added but never verified. 404 when nobody holds the domain, 409 with code already_yours or verified_elsewhere when it cannot be claimed. Requires the domain:read scope.
Resend-compatible. Removes the domain and its sending identity at the provider. Mail from it stops at once. Requires the domain:write scope and an owner or admin.
Retrieve details for a single domain including its current verification status and DNS records.
Return all sending domains associated with the current account.

operations.summary: Set up receiving DNS on Cloudflare in one click

Check whether the required DNS records have been configured correctly. If verification succeeds, the domain status changes to verified and it can be used for sending.
Cancel an email that has not been sent yet. Valid while the email is scheduled or queued; returns 409 once it has left for the provider. Requires the email:send scope.

Clicked links across all email over the last N days, ranked by clicks, with unique clicks (distinct emails). Pass url for one link's totals, daily series and the emails it was clicked in. Not in Resend, which lists clicked links per broadcast only. Requires the email:read scope.

operations.description: Resend-compatible counts and rates over a date range, for transactional and broadcast email together. Leave dimensions out for one totals row; add period, domain, email or broadcast (email and broadcast cannot be combined) to break the numbers down. Each lifecycle timestamp counts in its own period. Sends where every recipient is the SES mailbox simulator are left out. Rates are percentages with one decimal. Open and click metrics need tracking on. Requires the email:read scope.

queryParams.description: Comma-separated metrics to include. Omit for all.

The same URL is set on the RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe` header automatically.

operations.description: Organise one address on your own domain as an inbox with threads, labels, folders and drafts. The domain must have receiving turned on and be able to send (mail from the inbox is sent from its address): verified for sending, or a receiving subdomain of a verified domain. SMTPfast never provisions addresses on a shared domain, so forwarding: true is refused and receiving_address is always null. Mail the address already received in the last 30 days is filed into threads. Requires the domain:write scope on a key created by a team owner or admin.

fields.name: email_address
fields.description: A plain address on one of your domains, such as support@example.com

fields.name: forwarding
fields.description: Not available: must be false or omitted. Inboxes receive through your domain's MX record.

fields.name: name

operations.description: Create a draft for a person to review and send. Nothing is sent, so it needs only the inbound:read scope: give an agent a key without email:send and every message it writes waits here for approval. Omit thread_id for a new conversation; send thread_id and reply_to_email_id together for a reply (recipients are not copied, set to before sending). At least one of to, cc, bcc, subject, text or html must be non-empty; 50 recipients at most; subject up to 900 characters (Resend allows 2000; a longer subject could never be sent here). Returns 201 for a new draft, or 200 when an unsent reply draft for that message already exists, updated with the fields sent.

operations.description: Sends real email: the approval step for a draft. It goes out from the inbox address through the normal send path; a reply draft joins its thread with threading headers, a new conversation starts a thread in sent. The draft needs a recipient and a body (and a subject when it is not a reply). The send claims the draft on the version it read, so an edit cannot slip in while it runs. Not in Resend: pass the revision a person reviewed; if the draft changed since, nothing is sent and the answer is 409 with code draft_changed. Without a body this is Resend's call. Sending the same draft twice queues one email; a draft that was already sent returns 409. Requires the inbound:read and email:send scopes.

operations.description: The messages of a thread, received and sent together, oldest first (after walks newer, before walks older). Not in Resend: latest=true returns the newest page instead of the oldest, still oldest first within it, so has_more means older messages exist; page back with before. Received messages carry status and the SPF, DKIM, DMARC, spam and virus verdicts (not in Resend), so an agent can tell a spoofed or flagged message from a clean one. Reading does not mark anything read. Requires the inbound:read scope.

Send a reply to a received message through the normal send pipeline (credits, suppression, safety checks, webhooks). The reply is threaded with In-Reply-To and References and linked to the received message. From defaults to the receiving address when it can send (its domain is verified, or it is a receiving subdomain of a verified domain), otherwise to the same local part on the nearest verified parent domain with Reply-To set to the receiving address; pass from to pick another verified reply address. To defaults to the sender's Reply-To, then From. Requires the inbound:read and email:send scopes.
